title: The board at minute 45: a promo-code service, end to end
caption: A finished interview design: hot validate reads come from a cache, contended redeems are one atomic write, and analytics stays off the checkout path.

steps.text: Minute 5, scope agreed: marketers create campaigns; shoppers validate a code in the cart and redeem it at checkout; codes have usage limits; abuse is blocked; marketers see results. About 1 200 validates/s, 10× on Black Friday, ~25 redeems/s. Correctness on redeem beats latency.
Campaign path: a marketer defines the code, discount, dates and limits. The Campaign API writes the source of truth and invalidates the cached rule.
Validate is the hot read and only a preview: the Validate API answers from the code cache (rules plus an approximate remaining count) and reads the DB on a miss. It never changes a counter.
Redeem is the contended write: run the fraud check, then one atomic conditional update (uses < limit) in the same transaction as the order. Exactly one decision per use, no oversell.
Reporting is a requirement but not a latency one: each redemption is an event on a queue, and a worker aggregates per code per hour. Checkout never waits for analytics.
Wrap-up (minute 42): the first bottleneck is one hot code's counter row; the failure plan covers the cache and the DB; watch redeem p99, rejected redeems and fraud blocks.

scenarios.name: Black Friday spike
scenarios.summary: 10× validates are cheap cache reads, but one doorbuster code concentrates thousands of redeems on one row: that is the deep dive to offer.

steps.text: Midnight: validates jump to 12 000/s and a "first 10 000 orders" code goes live.
The gateway rate-limits per customer; validates are served from the cache.
2 000 redeem attempts/s hit the same code row: every update waits on one row lock.
Events spike too, but the queue absorbs them; stats lag by a minute.

scenarios.name: Code cache down
scenarios.summary: Validate degrades, redeem doesn't: the DB is the source of truth, so losing the cache costs latency and DB load, never correctness.

steps.text: The code-cache cluster fails during peak.
Validates fall through to the DB (read replicas): size them for the miss storm, or shed load.
Under pressure, the cart shows "code will be checked at checkout"; redeem still makes the real decision.

scenarios.name: Twist: one per customer
scenarios.summary: At minute 30 the interviewer adds "one use per customer". Absorb it at one box: a uniqueness constraint in the redeem transaction.

steps.text: Interviewer: "Each customer may use a code only once."
Redeem inserts (code_id, customer_id) into a redemptions table with a unique key, in the same transaction as the counter update.
A second attempt violates the key and fails cleanly. The fraud check catches one person with many accounts (device, card, address).
Say what didn't change: validate, campaigns and analytics.
